'''Platon Sergeevich Poretsky''' ({{langx|ru|Платон Серге́евич Порецкий}}; 3 October 1846 in [[Kirovohrad|Elisavetgrad]], [[Russian Empire]] – 9 August 1907 in [[Gorodnyansky Uyezd]], [[Chernigov Governorate]], Russian Empire) was a noted [[Russians|Russian]] Imperial [[astronomer]], [[mathematician]], and [[logician]].

Graduated from [[Kharkov University]], he worked in [[Astrakhan]] and [[Pulkovo Observatory|Pulkovo]] in [[St. Petersburg]].

Later, as an astronomer at [[Kazan University]], following the advice of his older colleague Professor of Mathematics A. V. Vasiliev at [[Kazan University]] (father of [[Nicolai A. Vasiliev]]) to learn the works of [[George Boole]], Poretsky developed "logical calculus" and through specific "logical equations" applied it to the [[theory of probability]]. {{anchor|BJSP}}Thus, he extended and augmented the works of logicians and mathematicians George Boole, [[William Stanley Jevons]] and [[Ernst Schröder (mathematician)|Ernst Schröder]] (known as Boole–Jevons–Schröder–Poretsky method).<ref name="Brusentsov-Vladimirova_1998"/> He discovered [[Poretsky's law of forms]]<ref name="Poretsky_1884"/> and gave the first general treatment of antecedent and consequent Boolean reasoning,<ref name="Poretsky_1898"/><ref name="Brown_2012"/> laying the groundwork for [[Archie Blake (mathematician)|Archie Blake]]'s work on the [[Blake canonical form]].{{Dubious|date=December 2023|reason=Poretsky did fundamental work in logic, but F.M. Brown's cited book does not claim that he laid the groundwork for the complete sum of prime implicants}}
